examples.problem_statement: What is the area of the region shown above? (The figure is an L-shaped region: a full rectangle of length 15 and width 8 sits on top of a further strip of length 9 and width 12 - 8, so the overall bounding rectangle measures 15 by 12 with a 6 by 4 corner removed.)

solution.operation: split the region into rectangle R and rectangle S
solution.result: area of region = area of R + area of S
solution.description: Cut the L-shaped region along the internal edge so it becomes two non-overlapping rectangles; the total area is then just the sum of the two rectangle areas.
Multiply the length 15 by the width 8 to get the area of rectangle R.
Find the width of rectangle S by subtracting the width already used by rectangle R from the overall width 12.
Multiply rectangle S's length 9 by the width 4 just found to get its area.
Add the two rectangle areas to get the area of the whole region.
Check with the book's second approach: take the full 15 by 12 rectangle and subtract the missing 6 by 4 corner rectangle; the same 156 confirms the decomposition.

key_reminders: The area of a rectangle is length times width.
A composite region can be split into non-overlapping rectangles whose areas add.
The same region can be handled by completing it to a full rectangle and subtracting the removed piece.
common_mistakes: Using the full overall width 12 for rectangle S instead of the leftover 12 - 8 = 4.
Using the full length 15 for the removed corner rectangle instead of 15 - 9 = 6.
Multiplying 15 by 12 and reporting 180 as the answer, forgetting the missing corner.

examples.problem_statement: In what time will Rs 6250 amount to Rs 6632.55 at 4 p.c. compound interest payable half-yearly?

solution.description: Write the compound interest equation using the half-yearly rate: the annual 4 percent is halved to 2 percent per period, and t counts half-yearly periods.
Divide both sides by the principal and clear the decimals so the left side is a plain fraction of whole numbers.
Reduce the fraction and recognise it as an exact cube of 51/50; matching the exponents on both sides gives the number of half-yearly periods.
Convert back from half-yearly periods to years by halving t, since compounding half-yearly replaced r by r/2 and t by 2t.

key_reminders: For half-yearly compounding, use rate r/2 per period and count 2t periods.
A = P(1 + r/100)^t with r and t taken per compounding period.
Reduce the amount-to-principal ratio to a fraction and match it against powers of the growth factor to read off the exponent.
common_mistakes: Using 4 percent per period instead of halving it to 2 percent for half-yearly compounding.
Reporting t = 3 as 3 years instead of dividing by 2 to get 3/2 years.
Failing to recognise 132651/125000 as (51/50)^3 and abandoning the exact match.

examples.problem_statement: Preliminary screening: look at the series and give the next term. 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, ?

solution.description: Subtract each term from the next to expose the difference pattern; the gaps are consecutive odd numbers.
Continue the odd-number pattern to get the difference that leads to the missing term.
Add that next difference to the last given term to produce the answer.
Confirm with the book's second approach: the terms are consecutive perfect squares, so the eighth term is 8 squared.

key_reminders: First-difference chains often reveal the rule at a glance.
Consecutive odd differences are the signature of a perfect-square series.
Preliminary screening: try recognising the pattern by sight before any calculation.
common_mistakes: Adding the last observed difference 13 again instead of advancing it to 15, giving 62.
Reading the series as 7^2 next and answering 49 twice, losing track of the term index.
